name: vehicle-task-states-visual
description: Visual check: vehicle state transitions through idle moving working and waiting states

steps.description: cash:100000 override (campaign.ts's own `cash:` knob, mirroring new_game's) replaces dusty_hollow's default $50,000: the file now buys a debris_hauler ($25,000, pre-existing idle/moving/working coverage) AND a drill_rig ($35,000, issue #550's driving-to-task coverage) plus a driller hire ($1,000) -- $61,000 minimum before any fuel/maintenance ticks, more than the level default allows regardless of purchase order. Terrain/seed/grid are untouched (level.terrainSeed still drives regenerateGrid), so every camera-calibrated coordinate elsewhere in this file stays valid.

Real click path: select hauler #1 in the 3D scene, rest the cursor on the destination, press the selection bar's MOVE HERE. The old description here claimed no UI drives this command and none should exist -- false since the SelectionBar gained `move_here` (G4), usable with a mouse since ScenePicking started latching `.aim` (47f4fef). DESTINATION CHANGED from (2,2) to (37,33): (2,2) sits in dusty_hollow's far corner behind a rise, and no camera-ray aim from the default orbit can land on it -- a focus sweep along x=2.5 jumps straight from tile z=0 to z=3, skipping 1 and 2, so the tile is occluded. This file tests idle -> moving -> transport task transitions, not one particular destination, so it aims at a tile a player can actually point at. (37,33) is the same tile vehicle-traffic-routing-visual drives to on this level, and its focus point was measured in a real browser until the dispatched command read `vehicle move 1 to:37,33`.

expect.note: vehicle list confirms idle → moving; no scalar field exists for vehicle task state

steps.description: Left unmarked: `vehicle assign <id> task:<task>` writes the VehicleTask enum straight onto the vehicle, skipping the drive/load/unload sequence ArrivalGate drives, so it reaches a state no real flow produces -- classified as a test-only state poke alongside `employee assign_skill` (gap G5). Every player-meaningful task has its own control: transport/loading -> Haul, clearing -> Break, moving -> the selection bar's MOVE HERE, which the step above now clicks.

expect.note: vehicle list confirms moving → transport, overriding the earlier move task

steps.description: Issue #550: a driller to claim the vehicle-gated dispatch below. Hired after the debris_hauler section so this file's earlier idle/moving/working coverage is untouched.

Left unmarked: hiring grants only the driller's starting 'blasting' qualification (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION, Employee.ts) -- the drill_rig licence (ROLE_LICENCE_REQUIRED, VehicleDriverAssignment.ts) is a separate grant. The player-facing path is `employee train`; this is the same bootstrap shortcut employee-skills-visual.json uses.

expect.note: blasting (from the driller role) + driving.drill_rig (the vehicle's required licence)

steps.command: employee dispatch 1 x:37 z:33 skill:blasting vehicle:drill_rig
steps.description: Left unmarked: no UI control drives `employee dispatch` and none should exist (see employee-skills-visual.json's identical note) -- this is the vehicle-gated dispatch path issue #550 wires up. requiredVehicleRole:drill_rig means the driller must claim a free licensed drill_rig, walk to it, board it, and ride it to (37,33) before the work timer starts -- claim/walk/board/drive/work is exactly the state sequence the driving-to-task-state shot below is meant to catch mid-drive.

interaction.command: employee dispatch 1 x:37 z:33 skill:blasting vehicle:drill_rig

steps.description: Async work: gives the driller time to walk to the drill_rig and board it before the next step inspects state — same tick-padding convention as survey-then-blast.json.

Further ticks to carry the boarded driller through the drive-to-target leg — the vehicle, not the employee, is what's still travelling here; taskTicksRemaining must not start until the vehicle itself reaches (37,33) (issue #550).

#922 visual evidence: mid-drive, wide-framed shot centred between the fleet's spawn/boarding cell and the dispatch target (37,33) the drill_rig is still driving toward. Before the fix, the driller's character mesh stayed parked at the boarding cell for the whole drive (EntitySync.syncEntitySets never suppressed it) while the drill_rig — with the driller supposedly aboard — drove off toward (37,33) alone; correct behaviour draws no separate character mesh at all here, only the vehicle. CAMERA RETARGETED after running this scenario through a real browser (#922 visual-tester pass): the debris_hauler's actual NavGrid-snapped spawn came back at (82,34) (dusty_hollow's world-centre raw spawn point gets pushed there by the corner-anchored reachability snap, not the raw baseX/baseZ formula), and by the tick this step runs the drill_rig has driven to roughly x∈[55,68] — the original x:43/distance:40 framing put the spawn cell just past the right edge of the canvas (occluded by the minimap widget), so it never actually proved the boarding cell was empty. x:60 z:34 distance:55 keeps both the (82,34) spawn cluster and the drill_rig's current position comfortably inside the frame with margin for further real-time drift during capture (sim keeps running in real time while the screenshot/orbit shots are taken).

Crew panel's task line should now read 'driving_to_task' (EmployeeActivityKind, EmployeeActivity.ts) rather than 'working' — the work timer only starts once the vehicle itself arrives at the target, not the employee boarding it. Reopens the Crew panel (same pattern as crew-fleet-panels-visual.json's observe steps): step 14's `vehicle buy drill_rig` switched the toolbar to the Fleet panel and nothing since has switched it back, so without this click the driving-to-task-state shot below would keep showing Fleet, never the Crew panel this file exists to demonstrate.
